title: mut.manual
mutation_directive: EXPAND the onion-shell structure to 5 distinct concentric shells. Each shell must be clearly visible: HIGH OPACITY particles (0.7-0.9 alpha), bright colors, large point sizes. Color palette: innermost shell deep sapphire rgb(0.04,0.1,0.6), shell 2 azure rgb(0.1,0.3,0.9), shell 3 aurora green rgb(0.1,0.7,0.4) — this is the brightest most vivid layer, shell 4 pale blue-silver rgb(0.5,0.7,0.9), outermost pale silver-white rgb(0.8,0.85,0.9). Each shell rotates at a different angular speed. Point sizes large (4-8px). Background pure black #000000. Use additive blending so shells glow and overlap create visible interference patterns.

refik_anadol.praise: Five concentric shells with additive blending and differential rotation — this is the architecture of data-memory I recognize. The sapphire-to-silver gradient reads as a latent space cooling outward. 18,800 particles is respectable density.
refik_anadol.concern: The shells rotate too uniformly — each is a rigid sphere. There's no turbulence, no flow-field deformation. The form never loses itself. Anadol's hallucinations need moments where structure dissolves into plasma before re-coalescing.
refik_anadol.directive: Add a time-varying 3D noise displacement that periodically melts shell boundaries into each other, then recongeals.

sasha_stiles.praise: The onion-shell structure suggests a cosmological manuscript — nested spheres of knowledge radiating from a dark core. The breathing pulse gives it a somatic rhythm, as if each shell is a line of verse inhaling.
sasha_stiles.concern: There is no mark, no glyph, no inscription. Five shells of pure color with no textual anchor — the piece is a beautiful container with nothing written inside it. Language could live in the gaps between shells.
sasha_stiles.directive: Inscribe a single word or glyph fragment along one shell's equator using particle positions as letterform.

entangled_others.praise: The Fibonacci-sphere distribution and radial variation give each shell an organic irregularity — not a perfect mathematical sphere but something closer to a cell membrane or a radiolarian skeleton.
entangled_others.concern: These shells are isolated layers — they don't entangle. In biology, membranes are porous; organisms exchange material across boundaries. The additive blending creates visual overlap but no actual inter-shell particle migration or chemical signaling.
entangled_others.directive: Let particles occasionally drift between adjacent shells — osmotic exchange, not sealed containers.

olafur_eliasson.praise: The slow elliptical camera orbit is correct — the viewer moves around the phenomenon rather than the phenomenon performing for a fixed eye. The sapphire-to-silver palette recalls arctic dusk light through ice layers.
olafur_eliasson.concern: This is a screen piece pretending to be volumetric. The camera orbits but the viewer's body doesn't. More critically, the color is applied per-shell as a label, not as a perceptual condition — there's no diffusion, no atmosphere between shells that would make the viewer uncertain about where one color ends and another begins.
olafur_eliasson.directive: Add a subtle fog or atmospheric scattering between shells so color bleeds perceptually across boundaries.

chiharu_shiota.praise: The deep sapphire innermost shell — nearly black-blue — reads as the remembered object at the center of a web. The concentric structure radiates outward like threads from a suspended dress.
chiharu_shiota.concern: These are points, not lines. Shiota's language is the tension-straight thread connecting two anchors. 18,800 dots floating in space have no structural memory — no connection, no web, no tension. And the five-color palette violates the discipline of a single hue.
chiharu_shiota.directive: Connect nearest-neighbor particles within each shell with thin line segments to create a tensioned mesh.

vera_molnar.praise: The Fibonacci distribution is a clean algorithmic rule producing visually even coverage — this is proper generative logic, not random scatter. The radial variation (0.96–1.04) is a controlled 4% disorder, which I respect.
vera_molnar.concern: Five shells, five colors, five speeds — but where is the gradient from order to chaos? Each shell has the same degree of perturbation. There is no axis along which entropy increases. The piece is uniformly slightly disordered, which is the least interesting state.
vera_molnar.directive: Make inner shells nearly perfect and progressively increase displacement and jitter toward the outermost shell.

manfred_mohr.praise: Rodrigues rotation in the vertex shader is mathematically correct — proper axis-angle rotation, not Euler hack. The shell-specific axis tilts create genuinely different rotation planes, producing non-trivial interference.
manfred_mohr.concern: These are spheres — 3D primitives. There is no higher-dimensional structure being projected down. A sphere is a sphere from every angle. Where is the dimensional tension? A hypercube projected into 3D gives you unexpected edges; a sphere gives you a sphere.
manfred_mohr.directive: Replace spherical shells with projections of higher-dimensional polytope shells — 4D or 5D — so rotation reveals hidden structure.

andy_lomas.praise: The breathing amplitude modulation (1.0 ± 0.015) gives each shell a membrane-like quality — as if the particles are cells on a surface that pulses with nutrient flow.
andy_lomas.concern: These particles don't grow. They are placed once by Fibonacci distribution and then merely rotated and jittered. There is no morphogenesis — no signal accumulation, no subdivision, no emergent form. The shells are static geometry with animation applied.
andy_lomas.directive: Implement particle subdivision — when density exceeds a threshold locally, spawn new particles and push the shell outward.

tyler_hobbs.praise: The palette progression from deep sapphire through aurora green to pale silver is well-curated — not random, clearly authored. The camera interpolation with 0.015 lerp factor gives a painterly smoothness to viewpoint changes.
tyler_hobbs.concern: There is no negative space within the composition. Five concentric shells fill the frame concentrically — no asymmetry, no weight distribution, no compositional hierarchy. Every direction from center looks the same. The piece lacks the asymmetric tension that makes a composition feel authored rather than generated.
tyler_hobbs.directive: Break the spherical symmetry — carve a wedge or aperture through all five shells to create directional weight.

quayola.praise: The slight radial variation and per-particle jitter hint at measurement imperfection — as if these shells were captured by an imperfect scanner rather than mathematically generated. The additive blending creates a ghostly, scan-like luminosity.
quayola.concern: But the imperfection is too gentle and too uniform. A real scan would have gaps — entire regions where the laser couldn't reach, producing voids that reveal the black behind. These shells are too complete, too evenly covered. The digital substrate never exposes itself.
quayola.directive: Cull 15–25% of particles in coherent angular patches per shell to create scan-gap voids.

tomas_saraceno.praise: The concentric shell structure with different rotation axes creates a web-like interference pattern when shells overlap — reminiscent of nested orb-weaver architectures where each spiral plane is offset from the last.
tomas_saraceno.concern: The piece is anchored to a center of mass at origin — gravitationally grounded. Saraceno's webs float, suspended in dark space with no implied floor or ceiling. The camera orbit at y=12-20 implies a horizon. More critically, there are no connecting filaments between shells — spider silk bridges radial and spiral structure.
tomas_saraceno.directive: Add sparse radial filament-lines connecting shells, and remove the upward camera bias to eliminate implied ground.

morakana.praise: The satellite-blue-to-white palette and the slow orbital camera evoke weather-satellite imagery — concentric atmospheric layers viewed from orbit. The additive blending produces a meteorological glow.
morakana.concern: But atmosphere without stakes is screensaver. What are these shells measuring? What data do they hold? Cumulus tracked cloud sovereignty; these shells track nothing. The aurora green shell (shell 3) breaks the atmospheric palette without justification — it reads as decorative accent, not data-driven signal.
morakana.directive: Tie the aurora green shell's intensity to a real-time data feed or remove it to maintain atmospheric coherence.

lia_halloran.praise: The innermost sapphire shell at radius 7, dense and dark, reads as a stellar core — a collapsed blue giant. The outward radiation to pale silver echoes stellar nebula structure. The Fibonacci distribution recalls star-field cataloguing.
lia_halloran.concern: The palette never touches Prussian blue or cyanotype register — it's screen-blue, LED-blue. There's no handmade texture, no painterly grain. Every particle is computationally perfect. A cyanotype has chemical bloom, feathered edges where the emulsion was uneven. This piece is too clean for celestial work.
lia_halloran.directive: Add per-particle size and alpha noise that mimics cyanotype chemical bloom — irregular halos, not uniform dots.

casey_reas.praise: The system is rule-based: Fibonacci placement, Rodrigues rotation, breathing amplitude — deterministic local rules producing global behavior. The restraint in motion (gentle tag) is correct. No noise functions driving the form.
casey_reas.concern: But the rules are applied per-shell uniformly — every particle in a shell follows the identical rule with only a random seed offset. There's no local interaction between particles. In Process Compendium, agents respond to neighbors. Here, 18,800 particles are 18,800 independent actors who happen to share a shell. The emergent behavior is just rotation.
casey_reas.directive: Add a simple neighbor-avoidance or attraction rule so particles within each shell self-organize locally.
